summary: A humorous article, dated September 25, 2023, about local entrepreneurs whose attempts to scale up their businesses go comically wrong, from overstocked yogurt to robotic cat toys and biodegradable bags that fall apart. Each vignette shows overconfidence or overestimated demand, but the owners stay cheerful. The article closes by celebrating dreamers who keep trying despite false starts.
one_line: A comic roundup of local business owners whose overambitious scaling-up efforts backfire, told with affectionate humor about optimism and overconfidence.
key_facts: The article is dated September 25, 2023 and compares local businesses scaling up to 'a fish climbs a tree'.
George Papadopoulos owns 'Ye Olde Greek Yogurt Emporium' and ordered enough containers to supply a small country, but townspeople preferred regular yogurt, leaving his living room full of stock.
Mildred 'Milly' Sanders gave her cat café 'Feline Good' a tech makeover with robots and virtual reality mouse chasers on October 15, 2023.
Mrs. Whiskerson the tabby rejected the mechanical mouse and defected to the café next door, taking half of Milly's clientele.
Alfred 'Alfie' Mckenzie held a street fashion show of his retro neon clothing line on November 3, 2023; the only orders came from confused tourists who thought it was performance art.
Alfie Mckenzie insists 'Neon's the new black', and his fashion line now doubles as emergency road signage.
Donna 'The Risotto Maestro' Giovannini quadrupled her kitchen staff overnight on September 16, 2023, and accidentally created a dish called 'Burnt to a Crispini'.
Arnold 'Arnie' Thompson runs the 'Eco-Friendly Everything' store and invested in 100% biodegradable shopping bags that decomposed when filled with groceries.
By December 21, 2023, Arnie Thompson was often seen chasing rolling oranges down the street, and his customers now bring their own reusable bags.
Bob 'Just Bob' Stevenson, owner of 'Bob's Building Bonanza', unveiled his expanded hardware store on January 10, 2024.
Bob Stevenson's stock of 4-in-1 multimix cement and left-handed screwdrivers has little local demand, and local kids use the surplus for obstacle courses.
The article concludes that scaling up is like starting a rock band in a garage: noisy, with false starts, but worth laughing about.
